what: review-accepted: the acceptance record is the review page's Accept hand-off for the spec at the registered commit, read by octo-feather-accepted from every session's registry rows and their spools.
why: Nothing writes the registry's accepted registration the spec named, so the owner's Accept was never recorded (PR #56, owner approved 2026-10-20).
evidence: Pilot 1 (2026-10-20): Tom pressed Accept spec, the page wrote its hand-off, and octo-feather-accepted still exited 1 waiting for a registry accepted = true that nothing writes; the agent hand-wrote it twice.

what: LINEAR_API_KEY comes only from the environment, herdr-spawn passes it into panes, nothing stores or logs it and the qc judge runs without it; just install-check checks the linear CLI for a Linear target. Adds acceptance-linear-key-panes, -qc, acceptance-install-linear, story-tracker-key and story-tracker-tools.
why: Owner ruling (2026-10-22, issue #82): the kit works with Linear directly so it can run on a Linear-first repository; the tracker is set per target in .octo-feather.toml, tracker work lives in packaged skills (github-pr, github-issues, linear) behind fixed script names, and ADR 0004 and 0011 were corrected in place to match.
evidence: Corrected ADR 0004 says the tracker is GitHub Issues or Linear, chosen per target, and ADR 0011 that a Linear lane's key is its lowercased ticket key, while the spec as accepted says a toolchain of 'git, gh, jq, just, python3, uv, node, pnpm, Herdr and Pi' and no tracker key (host-tools); the accepted criteria cannot pass on a Linear target.

what: The linear CLI on the box is schpet/linear-cli at the release the vendored skill is pinned to (v3.1.0), from its release binary or npx @schpet/linear-cli, authenticated by LINEAR_API_KEY; the install check names the pinned version and how to install it.
why: Owner direction (2026-10-22, issue #82, before Accept): schpet/linear-cli (ISC, release v3.1.0), the CLI octo-lite uses, ships its own agent skill; vendor it and keep the kit's linear tracker skill to the seven fixed scripts as thin CLI wrappers.
evidence: host-tools pointed install to 'the linear skill's install notes', which the linear skill no longer holds (skills local-linear: only the tracker scripts), while the vendored linear-cli SKILL.md gives the install path: 'npx @schpet/linear-cli' or the release install.

what: Adds the headless browser to the box toolchain, installed once outside the cache folder the qc sandbox masks, and an install check criterion for it.
why: The qc sandbox mounts a tmpfs over ~/.cache, so a browser installed there is invisible to the judge; one box-wide install read by every agent and the judge avoids a 681 MB install per target.
evidence: Issue #136 spike (comment 6399339214, evidence /tmp/gh136-spike/evidence): q2-run1.log: inside scripts/octo-feather-qc-sandbox Playwright failed with 'Executable doesn't exist' because ~/.cache is masked; q2-run2.log passed once the browsers sat outside ~/.cache with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH set. remote#host-tools lists no browser.

what: The box toolchain includes agent-browser at the vendored skill's release with a browser it can start, and just install-check lists it when missing or at another version. Adds acceptance-install-browser.
why: Owner ruling (2026-10-27, issue #256): implementers and correctors drive a real browser through agent-browser's CLI, so the box must have it at the release its skill is pinned to.
evidence: remote#host-tools lists the box toolchain without agent-browser, against skills#loading-agent-browser (this lane) requiring the CLI at the skill's pinned release; `which agent-browser` on the box: not found.

what: This lane's owner-accepted remote criterion and story (accepted at e02cc63 as acceptance-install-browser, story-browser-tools) are renamed acceptance-install-agent-browser and story-agent-browser-tools, text unchanged but the story naming agent-browser, beside #136's same-id criterion and story (Playwright headless Chromium for a target's verify skill, built in PR 181); host-tools carries both clauses. Adds acceptance-install-agent-browser; supersedes this lane's 2026-10-28T01:17:31Z remote call, whose acceptance-install-browser now names #136's criterion.
why: Merging origin/main 2b2fab5 (#181, lane gh136) into gh256: both lanes added remote anchors acceptance-install-browser and story-browser-tools with different meanings, each accepted by the owner separately (#136 at cbd9bfa, this lane at e02cc63); an anchor lives once, so this lane's planned pair moves to new ids and #136's built pair stays.
evidence: git merge origin/main: CONFLICT docs/specs/remote.spec.html; origin/main remote.spec.html acceptance-install-browser 'a target whose verify skill drives a headless browser ... naming the version the target pins' (built, pr 181) against gh256 e02cc63 acceptance-install-browser 'a box without agent-browser ... naming the release the kit's agent-browser skill is pinned to' (planned).

what: host-vm: where the factory runs, whether a dedicated machine, and what needs exe.dev are ADR 0005's (pointer only); the row keeps the host requirement the kit checks: Linux with a kernel of 6.6 or later and unprivileged user namespaces, the qc sandbox's need. context: the lede points to ADR 0005 for where the factory runs and says exe.dev's proxy keeps review private where it is used.
why: Owner rulings at the #480 merge asks (2026-10-30, verbatim): "no the factory can run anywhere, it's just that we decided to use a remote box for this exact session"; "those need to be changed too. this factory can run anywhere the user wants it to run"; "it preferrably has it's own server, but doesn't have to". Earlier, owner field report on issue #422 (comment 2): a non-exe.dev Debian box ran the factory with owner approval; the qc sandbox needs the kernel and user namespaces (#404).
evidence: remote#host-vm said only 'One exe.dev VM ... Ubuntu' and the lede 'The factory runs on one dedicated VM', against the owner's ruling above and the owner's Debian box (issue #422 comment 2, item 1) reaching a green GATE_WORKERS=1 just check (65 passed, comment 4); octo-feather-qc runs under `unshare -rm` (octo-feather-qc --help), which needs unprivileged user namespaces.

what: host-tools: agent-browser's browser outside the masked cache; the gate Python pinned by the kit, owned by uv, installed without ~/.local/bin links; box python3 3.11+ for scripts; one pnpm store for test copies on another filesystem; just install-check checks everything a fresh box needs (toolchain, kernel and user namespaces, kit install on main, state folder, review service, role models), printing the exact fix per gap, naming a shadowing launcher, or the one manual step (exe.dev Private sharing); README is a short bootstrap ending in install-check and one full just check. host-models: install-check calls each role model once and reports a rejected key plainly, never printing it.
why: Issue #422 (owner request 2026-10-29): a fresh box must be set up by an agent from the repo alone, install-check being the runbook; owner field reports (comments 2 and 3, items 2 to 10); owner ruling via director 2026-10-30: gate Python pinned through uv (.python-version 3.12.15, `uv python install --no-bin`), not mise, per the #261 one-owner-per-tool ruling; system python3 >= 3.11 stays allowed for kit scripts.
evidence: just install-check on HEAD 2cac117 prints bare 'MISSING' for herdr, gh, jq, git, python3 and checks no kernel, user namespaces, review service, model, kit install or state folder (justfile install-check recipe); issue #422 comment 2: older launchers shadowed mise/node/pnpm/uv, pnpm used an empty /tmp store, a prebuilt Python lacked os.pidfd_open and Debian's lacked venv, a rejected proxy key surfaced late, agent-browser's Chrome sat under the masked cache; the kit pins no Python (no .python-version; pyproject requires-python >=3.10).

what: The per-role model check is a separate setup check the runbook names (just install-check-models), not part of just install-check, so routine install-check runs (post-merge step 3 after every merge, gates) make no model call; host-tools' install-check list drops 'each role model'.
why: Director design ruling 2026-10-30: post-merge step 3 runs just install-check after every merge; a default probe would make a real call per role model per merge (spend, latency, provider flakiness stopping the routine). Narrows this lane's own earlier 2026-10-30 host-tools/host-models call before any build.
evidence: scripts/octo-feather-lane post-merge step 3 runs `just install-check <the current repo's top>` after every merge (octo-feather-lane --help, post-merge); remote#host-models (68aab91) put the model call in just install-check itself.

what: host-vm points to ADR 0005 (the one owner of where the factory runs and what needs exe.dev) instead of restating it, keeping only the host requirement the spec owns.
why: Code review of PR #480 (bad9c3b and bb18cbc, blocking, duplicated-rule, docs/adr/0008 rung 1): the spec restated ADR 0005's host rule. Text follows the owner's 2026-10-30 rulings ("those need to be changed too. this factory can run anywhere the user wants it to run").
evidence: docs/specs/remote.spec.html:62 at bad9c3b and docs/adr/0005-dedicated-remote-host.md:3 both said exe.dev is needed only for review hosting and the model proxy and the rest runs on any dedicated Linux box with kernel 6.6+ and unprivileged user namespaces (review finding, class duplicated-rule).

what: Removes every place rule: acceptance-vm-only (the owner's laptop runs no agent), story-dedicated and host-never-laptop are removed; the lede, section heading, table caption and boundary-vm speak of the host, and an exe.dev VM only where its review proxy or model proxy is used; host-models: model calls use the provider configuration Pi has on the host, on exe.dev the deployment's model proxy. A dedicated machine is recommended, never required: ADR 0005 owns it. remote.status.json drops acceptance-vm-only.
why: Owner rulings, verbatim, 2026-10-30: "those need to be changed too. this factory can run anywhere the user wants it to run" and "it preferrably has it's own server, but doesn't have to" (owner-authorized weakening, relayed by the director; the only remaining host limit is the technical requirement install-check checks).
evidence: remote.spec.html at bb18cbc: acceptance-vm-only ('the owner's laptop runs no agent of the factory'), story-dedicated ('agents never run on my laptop'), host-never-laptop ('The owner's laptop runs no agent, Herdr session or toolchain') and the lede ('This deployment runs the factory on one dedicated VM') restrict where the factory runs, against the owner rulings quoted.

what: host-tools lists bubblewrap and socat as box tools the qc sandbox's maintained agent sandbox needs (sandbox-runtime, pinned and installed by the kit with its own node packages). Criteria named are the toolchain row's install-check criteria, unchanged (no remote criterion names bubblewrap or socat; the sandbox criterion is quality#acceptance-qc-sandbox-maintained).
why: The qc sandbox now runs on anthropics/sandbox-runtime, which on Linux needs bubblewrap and socat on the box (#689); the toolchain row is the one owner of what a box must have, and install-check already checks both.
evidence: remote#host-tools listed git, gh, jq, just, python3, uv, node, pnpm, Herdr and Pi but neither bubblewrap nor socat, while PR #698's install-check prints 'bwrap ok (srt, the qc sandbox, needs it)' and 'socat ok' and the sandbox fails without them (srt README: Linux needs bwrap and socat).

what: host-tools lists bubblewrap, socat and ripgrep (rg) as host dependencies of the qc sandbox's maintained agent sandbox. Criteria unchanged; these are the toolchain row's existing install-check criteria, and the sandbox criterion is quality#acceptance-qc-sandbox-maintained.
why: The pinned sandbox-runtime requires rg on Linux as well as bubblewrap and socat. A host provisioned from the documented toolchain without rg cannot initialize that sandbox. Extends the existing host-tools/install-check prerequisite mechanism, not a second mechanism.
evidence: GitHub Actions run 42504969341, exact code head 4d97857377bacbe24a23d6c078b9c81e0277d490, check job Run just check: Error: Sandbox dependencies not available: ripgrep (rg) not found. Pinned @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime 0.0.81 dist/sandbox/sandbox-manager.js checkDependenciesCommon (lines 1216-1230) checks rg and reports its absence; remote#host-tools named only bubblewrap and socat.
